sources.entry: LinuxCNC - Linux based CNC machine controller. It can drive milling machines, lathes, 3D printers, laser cutters, plasma cutters, robot arms, hexapods, and more. (Source Code) GPL-2.0/LGPL-3.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: LinuxCNC is a Linux-based software controller for driving CNC machines such as mills, lathes, 3D printers, laser and plasma cutters, robot arms, and hexapods.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LinuxCNC as software for controlling CNC machines, stating it can drive milling machines, lathes, 3D printers, laser cutters, plasma cutters, robot arms, hexapods, and more. It has been developed for about 25 years with contributions from many countries. Since release 2.9 the documentation has been translated through the Weblate crowd translation service, and users are invited to contribute translations. The README itself is short and links to a website, install instructions, build instructions, and documentation, but does not detail specific features beyond the machine types listed. It includes a safety disclaimer stating the authors accept no liability and that software alone should not be relied on for safety.
how_to_run: See the Install and Build links in the README (external documentation; no commands given in the README)
notable: Linux-based real-time machine controller for many machine types
Project active for about 25 years with international contributors
Documentation translated via Weblate crowd translation
caveats: README warns that machinery must have independent power-removal provisions and that software alone should not be relied on for safety
Authors disclaim liability and responsibility for machinery safety compliance
Installation and build details are only on external documentation pages, not in the README
